answers.core: It's not rare to have strings longer than 100 chars, be it log messages or game dialogue. Why waste CPU power to concatenate when one string do trick?
answers.workaround:
You can concatenate the strings:
```GDScript
func _ready() -> void:
	var s := "Hello this is a normal" +
			"two line string, " +
			"that stretches over three lines."
```

You could also use something like:
```GDScript
func _ready() -> void:
	var s := "Hello this is a normal
			two line string.".replace("\t", "").replace("\n", " ")
```
Although you lose the ability to add escape sequences yourself.

title: Ignore tabs and newlines added by formatting for multiline strings and raw strings
